title: WWII Sabotage Spotlight: Operation Gunnerside
summary: Josh and Chuck return from a long break to cover Operation Gunnerside, the 1943 Norwegian resistance sabotage of the Vemork heavy water plant that set back Nazi atomic bomb research. They cover heavy water's role as a nuclear moderator, Norway's invasion and resistance, Leif Tronstad and the SOE training of Norwegian saboteurs, the failed Operation Freshman gliders, the Gunnerside raid led by Joachim Rønneberg, the later Allied bombing, the sinking of the ferry Hydro in February 1944 with its heavy water barrels, and the debate over the operation's impact. The episode ends with a listener mail from Justin Meeks about Tavern on the Green and David Letterman, and an announcement that the hosts are not doing live shows in 2025.

segments.title: Welcome back and episode setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck greet listeners after a long break and introduce the topic of Operation Gunnerside, suggested by listener Matthew.

segments.title: Nuclear fission race and heavy water
segments.summary: The hosts explain how fission discovery sparked a race for an atomic bomb, and why heavy water (deuterium oxide) was a useful neutron moderator for the Germans, while the US chose graphite.

segments.title: Leif Tronstad and the Vemork plant
segments.summary: Chemist Leif Tronstad, who produced small amounts of heavy water at the Vemork plant in Telemark for Norsk Hydro, is introduced, and the plant's heavy water role is described.

segments.title: German invasion of Norway and resistance
segments.summary: Norway's neutrality ends with the German invasion in April 1940, followed by Nazi rule, strikes, martial law, and Norwegians resisting from within and abroad.

segments.title: Tronstad in London and SOE training
segments.summary: Tronstad escapes to the UK, trains saboteurs with the Special Operations Executive, and keeps in contact with allies at the plant. The Scotland training and the Vemork terrain are described.

segments.title: Bombing plan rejected and Company Linge
segments.summary: Americans propose bombing the plant, but Tronstad argues against it due to civilian risk and the plant's value. Company Linge is formed and Operation Swallow launched under Jens Anton Poulsen.

segments.title: Operation Freshman gliders and Operation Gunnerside begins
segments.summary: Operation Freshman's two gliders crash and the survivors are executed by the Gestapo. Joachim Rønneberg is then chosen to lead the smaller Operation Gunnerside team.

segments.title: Team's approach through the gorge
segments.summary: Nine saboteurs gather and trek forty miles in February. Rønneberg's bolt cutters get them through the fence, and they avoid the bridge and minefield by descending a gorge.

segments.title: Infiltration and explosives at Vemork
segments.summary: Two saboteurs enter via a cable shaft after an inside contact fails to leave a door open. They subdue a watchman, the other team enters through a window, and charges are set with a shortened fuse. Only a small pop is heard and the guards go back to bed.

segments.title: Escape and immediate outcome
segments.summary: All nine saboteurs escape without firing a shot or killing anyone.

segments.title: Escape to Sweden and Allied bombing of Vemork
segments.summary: The saboteurs ski to Sweden. The Nazis restart production within months, and the Allies bomb the plant in a later raid that kills twenty-two Norwegian civilians. The Nazis then move heavy water production to Germany.

segments.title: Sinking of the ferry Hydro
segments.summary: Company Linge's Knut Haukelid leads an attack on the ferry Hydro in February 1944, sinking it with heavy water aboard. Fourteen Norwegian civilians and four Germans die. A 2003 PBS Nova salvage proved the barrels contained heavy water.

segments.title: Impact debate and the graphite miscalculation
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the operation's impact, the Nazi atomic program's flawed choice of heavy water, and a miscalculation about graphite that the Allies never learned of.

segments.title: Film, Norwegian broadcast, and Tronstad's death
segments.summary: The 1965 film The Heroes of Telemark is mentioned, along with the 2015 NRK miniseries The Heavy Water War. Tronstad's later Operation Sunshine and his death in May 1945 are described.

segments.title: Episode title discussion
segments.summary: The hosts mention Olivia's suggested title for the episode and thank her.

segments.title: Listener mail: Tavern on the Green and David Letterman
segments.summary: Listener Justin Meeks shares his grandmother's Thanksgiving dinner with David Letterman at Tavern on the Green. The hosts also announce they will not do live shows in 2025, including SketchFest.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing credits for Stuff You Should Know.
